### Test a three-second character replacement


Upload a short source clip and an authorized reference image, then inspect the subject, motion, clothing, and background across the entire result.


[Try Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace)


You have a video with the right action, but the wrong character. Starting the scene again may mean losing the movement or background you wanted to keep.


Before you try another tool, decide whether you need to change the whole subject or only the face. This guide walks you through replacing a character with your own reference image, beginning with a short representative clip. You’ll learn which inputs to prepare, what to inspect in the result, and how to choose between Replace, Animate and a more focused face swap.

## **What You Can Make With Character Replace**


- Turn your own performance into an original cartoon, anime character or mascot.
- Explore casting or costume concepts using footage and reference images you are authorized to edit.
- Create character variants for a clearly presented creative scene.
- Adapt an approved presenter shot while reviewing the new character and keeping any spoken claims accurate.


## **What You Need Before You Start**


Before generating your first video, prepare a few simple assets to get the best results.


- A short source video with one clearly visible subject. Start with three seconds for the guest workflow.
- A sharp reference image that shows the intended character’s face and clothing.
- A supported browser and an internet connection.
- A defined goal: replace the subject in the video, or animate the character using the source motion.


For a longer project, inspect the duration, resolution and credit quote in your account before generating. The three-second guest example is not the maximum for every paid workflow.


## **How to Replace a Character in a Video With AI: Step by Step**


### **Step 1: Open Magic Hour's Character Replace Tool**


Go to the[Magic Hour Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) tool in your browser. You can start creating immediately without signing up, making it one of the quickest ways to test AI character replacement.


### **Step 2: Upload Your Source Video**


Upload one continuous shot with a visible subject and steady lighting. Start with a three-second sample in the guest tool. Trim unrelated scenes before generation, and check the available duration and output settings for a longer signed-in project.


Avoid videos with rapid scene changes, heavy motion blur, or extremely dark lighting, as these can make it harder for the AI to maintain a stable character throughout the clip.


### **Step 3: Choose Your Reference Character**


Next, decide who or what will replace the original subject. You have two options:


- Upload a reference image of a person, illustrated character or mascot you are authorized to use.
- Where available, select a built-in reference or preset to explore the workflow.


For commercial work, use an approved character or performer. Paying for generation does not by itself grant rights to a celebrity’s likeness or a third party’s fictional character.


Use a sharp reference that shows the features and clothing you want preserved. A close crop of a face gives less information about the full body or outfit than an appropriate wider reference.


### Step 4: Choose Replace or Animate, then generate


Choose **Replace** when the person in the source video should become the reference character. Choose **Animate** when the source video should drive the motion of the character image. Review the selected settings, then start generation.


### Watch the replacement and animation routes


This official Magic Hour walkthrough demonstrates replacing a person in footage and animating a reference image. Match the recorded route to your starting input, then review the full result for changes to the subject and scene. Current modes and controls can differ from the recording.


Source:[Magic Hour AI: How to Replace a Person in a Video & Animate Any Image with AI | Magic Hour](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eS3dqwxowvY)


#### Choose which person changes in the signed-in workflow


The guest tool is a quick way to try Replace or Animate. For explicit subject selection, open the[signed-in Character Replace editor](https://magichour.ai/create/character-replace) . Add the clip under Video to edit and the reference under Character to use. Choose Select person, move the filmstrip to a frame where the intended subject is visible, click or tap that person, and confirm Select This Person. Auto leaves the selection to the tool.


Set the trim before confirming the subject. If you change it afterwards, check your selection points again: points outside the selected segment are excluded. If every point is outside the range, select the person again inside the new trim or adjust the segment. These dashboard steps are documented in the[Character Replace step-by-step guide](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/16917099-character-replace-step-by-step-guide) .


**Check targeting separately from appearance.** If the wrong person changes, revisit the selected subject and trim before generating another variant. If the intended person changes but the outfit or silhouette is wrong, revisit the replacement image and the whole-character workflow. Approve the entire short result, including moments when people cross or the subject turns; a correct first frame does not establish that the rest of the clip is correct.


Generation time varies with the source clip, model, settings, and queue load. Wait for a completed result and inspect it before exporting; a fixed 30-to-60-second turnaround is not guaranteed.


### **Step 5: Review the Result**


When generation finishes, compare the output with your original video. Check whether:


- Does the replacement keep a recognizable identity throughout the clip?
- Do the limbs, hands and clothing remain coherent during movement?
- Does the background behave as expected for Replace mode?
- Are the original timing, camera movement and any dialogue suitable for the finished scene?


Start with steady movement and consistent lighting so the source character is easier to track. Review difficult frames such as turns, occlusions, and motion blur.


### **Step 6: Download or Create More Variations**


If you’re happy with the result, download your video. Free video generations include a watermark. Paid subscriptions and credit-pack purchases include watermark-free exports and commercial-use rights, subject to the source assets and the Terms. Subscription-only settings still depend on your account.


One of the easiest ways to experiment is by keeping the same source video and simply changing the reference character. This lets you quickly generate multiple versions without uploading the video again, making it easy to compare different characters for social media, marketing, or creative projects.


## **Tips for the Best Results**


Use these practical input and review guidelines to reduce avoidable problems. They are not a guarantee of a particular result or a reported controlled test:


- Start with one visible subject, steady lighting and a short continuous shot.
- Match the reference image to the character details you need in the output.
- Avoid fast cuts and heavy obstruction in the first sample.
- Choose Replace to change the subject in the existing shot; choose Animate for motion transfer.
- Review the full clip, especially turns, crossings and rapid gestures, before trying more variants.


## Replace vs Animate: which mode should you choose?


Magic Hour’s current controls use **Replace** and **Animate** . These correspond to different goals; choose the mode before generating.


**Replace** uses the reference character to replace the detected subject in the source video. It is the starting point when you want to keep the shot’s setting and performance while changing the person’s appearance. Inspect the boundaries and background in the actual result.


**Animate** transfers movement from the source video to the character image. Use it when the character image is the scene you want to bring into motion, rather than treating it as a simple face replacement.


For this tutorial’s goal—replacing a person in existing footage—start with Replace. A different character size, silhouette or movement can still expose artifacts, so approve a short sample before committing more credits.


## **What to Try Next**


To make the replaced character follow new dialogue, supply a finished audio track to[Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) . It synchronizes mouth movement in the existing video to that recording. If you start with a script or voice-cloning reference, finish and listen to the generated speech first. Review timing, pauses and identity across the complete result.


If you only want to change a person's face while keeping their original body and clothing,[Face Swap Video](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap/video) is a better fit.


To create a new scripted ad rather than replace a performer in existing footage, use[Magic Hour's AI UGC Ad Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-ugc-ad-generator) . Choose or upload an actor image, set the opening shot and product, then supply the approved script. For localization, change the script language and phrasing; support varies by model, so preview the full result before publishing.


## Diagnose a wrong replacement before another attempt


Magic Hour publishes this guide and includes its own product in the comparison. Treat the recommendations as editorial guidance from a vendor, and verify the linked first-party product details and your own output requirements before choosing a tool.


Check status first. For a signed-in job, open My Library; for a no-signup attempt, keep the exact tool page open and check its result area. Still processing is not the same as failed: avoid submitting it again. For a failed job, check the balance after failure processing. A completed but unchanged, blank or technically broken output needs review; a result you dislike is not an automatic credit return. See[generation status and credits](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/15011080-generation-failed-stalled-canceled-or-produced-a-blank-result-what-happens-to-credits) .


Illustrative targeting check: two performers cross in a shot, and the wrong one changes. In the signed-in editor, inspect Auto versus Select person before changing the reference image. Set the final trim, choose a frame where the intended performer is distinguishable, select that person and confirm. If you changed the trim after selecting, recheck that selection points remain inside it. For the next completed result, verify both performers through the crossing; reject a take that changes the uninvolved person.


If the intended person changes but the costume does not, inspect the replacement image next. Does it show the outfit you actually need? Confirm the whole-character workflow rather than a face-only change. Change one input or setting at a time and review the full clip. A clear reference still does not guarantee exact clothing, body shape or identity in every frame.


If the result remains wrong, keep the project and request review rather than repeatedly submitting the same inputs. Include the project link or visible ID, tool route, approximate time, Auto or Select person, selected points, trim, replacement image and the output timestamp where the replacement is incorrect or missing. If a guest attempt has no project ID, send its exact route and time. The[Character Replace support checklist](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/16917099-character-replace-step-by-step-guide) identifies the details needed for this workflow.


**Try the workflow:**[Open Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) . Use the same representative input and acceptance criteria before comparing results.
